messages:
Nadia (Customer): Hi team — we're seeing the streaming responses stop mid-generation and then sometimes the client gets the same tokens again after reconnect. This is hitting our product tests, and it's making outputs duplicated.
Alex (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro? client code + headers?
Nadia (Customer): here's a simplified repro. we open an EventSource to /v1/stream, stream chunks for ~2s, then we simulate a network blip. on reconnect we do a fresh GET with the same conversation id. sometimes the response restarts and we get the last 3 tokens repeated.
Nadia (Customer): logs: 
```
client: recv chunk: "...hello world"
client: connection closed (code=1006)
client: reconnecting with conversation_id=conv-42
client: recv chunk: "... world"    <-- duplicate
```
Alex (Support): ty. what's the SSE code you're using? any idempotency header?
Nadia (Customer): using EventSource polyfill in node. we don't set an explicit idempotency-key. we tried sending `X-Resume-Token` = last_event_id but no change.
Alex (Support): ok assigning to eng-oncall. @eng-oncall can you triage? I've flagged as P2 because customer is impacted in CI.
support-bot: Auto-escalation created: INC-2026-7890 (P2) — alerting eng-oncall
eng-oncall: looking. can you share server request ids for one of the sessions? we need the stream_id or request_id to correlate logs.
Nadia (Customer): one example: request_id=rsq_8f3b2a, stream_id=sid_210. here's the rough timeline: connect -> partial tokens streamed -> abrupt close after 2.1s -> reconnect with same conv id -> repeated tokens.
Priya (SRE): pulling logs for rsq_8f3b2a... I see a connection drop: `tcp FIN` at 2026-06-24T14:02:11Z, downstream client closed unexpectedly. Server stream state shows `last_sent_index=142`, `resume_supported=true`, `resume_cursor=141`. Then on the resumed request I see a new server-side request created `rsq_8f3b2b` with `resume_cursor=0` and assigned a new `generation_id`. That explains duplication — resume semantics weren't honored.
Miguel (Backend): thanks Priya. why was resume_cursor reset to 0? we have resume token lookup in the connection handler. looking at code: 
```
// simplified
if (headers['X-Resume-Token']) {
  const token = validateToken(headers['X-Resume-Token']);
  if (token && token.stream_id === req.stream_id) {
    req.resume_cursor = token.cursor;
  } else {
    req.resume_cursor = 0; // safe fallback
  }
}
```
Miguel (Backend): maybe the token validation failed because the token was expired (we TTL tokens to 30s). does client wait longer?
Nadia (Customer): in our case the blip was 45s. we expected resume to work for at least a few minutes.
Priya (SRE): aha — TTL mismatch. server intended short-lived resume tokens to avoid replays, but that causes customer pain for transient network issues. we can raise TTL but need to consider replay risk.
Alex (Support): customer also reported duplicate billing events — their logs show two billed requests for the resumed session. can eng check billing attribution?
Miguel (Backend): billing records tie to request_id. because the resumed reconnect created new request_id (rsq_8f3b2b) we charged twice. we can change attribution to detect resume and merge usage for N seconds.
eng-oncall: proposed short-term fixes: 
- increase resume token TTL to 5 minutes
- server should prefer resume cursor from a persisted resume store if token validation fails but stream_id matches and reconnect arrives within a safe window
- dedupe billing if `original_request_id` header present and `resume=true`

Priya (SRE): I'll roll a config change to the resume TTL flag to 5m in Canary region, monitor errors and billing.
Miguel (Backend): code follow-up: also add a defensive check so the runtime doesn't regenerate `generation_id` when `resume=true`. current bug path regenerates new generation_id which causes duplicate output because new generator starts from scratch.
Alex (Support): great. Nadia, we'll try to reduce disruption: can you set client to send last_event_id as `X-Resume-Token` (server expects base64 JSON {stream_id, cursor, issued_at})? here's sample: 
```
// client side
const resume = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({stream_id: 'sid_210', cursor: 142, issued_at: Date.now()})).toString('base64');
fetch('/v1/stream', {headers: {'X-Resume-Token': resume}})
```
Nadia (Customer): ok will try that and report back. thanks. also: what's recommended retry/backoff behavior?
Priya (SRE): backoff: jittered exponential starting at 200ms, max 10s, and only attempt resume if elapsed < 5min (matches TTL). if reconnect attempts exceed 6, open a new session.
Alex (Support): follow-ups:
- SRE to deploy TTL bump to 5m in canary (Priya)
- Backend to add generation_id preservation and billing dedupe logic (Miguel)
- Support to provide customer-friendly retry snippet and monitor (Alex)
- eng-oncall to watch INC-2026-7890 and escalate if errors spike (eng-oncall)

support-bot: INC-2026-7890 updated: progress noted — assigned to Miguel and Priya
Nadia (Customer): I applied the header change and simulated network blips up to 2m — resume worked reliably and duplicates stopped. thanks all. :rocket:
Alex (Support): awesome. leaving this open for a few days, will close when canary changes are stable and billing dedupe is in place. :thumbsup:
